statement: a diffusion-reaction model of ALD adapted to radial transport and adsorption in a porous particle, with a shape factor for the slab, cylinder and sphere
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the reactant front is one-dimensional in a slab but closes in from two and three dimensions in a cylinder and a sphere, so these need less exposure for full penetration
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: a sensitivity analysis ranks porosity and tortuosity, pore diameter, specific surface area, pore volume, particle radius, reactant molar mass, GPC, sticking probability, exposure and temperature by their effect on the penetration depth
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the model serves the design of ALD on porous media: catalyst particles as spheres, membranes as slabs, fibres and monoliths as cylinders
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the effective diffusion coefficient of a porous catalyst particle is the Knudsen coefficient times porosity over tortuosity, so it depends on pore size, temperature, molar mass, porosity and tortuosity
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the shape factor s = a − 1, with a the outer surface over volume times R, is 0, 1 and 2 for slab, cylinder and sphere; r runs from the outer surface (0) to the centre or mid-plane (R)
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: transport is taken as pure Knudsen diffusion, the mean free path far above the pore size, so the molecular term of the Bosanquet relation is dropped
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: adsorption is irreversible single-site Langmuir; the site area s0 is the reciprocal of the areal site density σ, which the GPC fixes
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: for the same exposure the coating penetrates deeper in the order sphere > cylinder > slab; the slab's reactant density falls linearly, the others' profiles curve
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the cylinder factor holds for long cylinders; a cylinder of height nR has s = 2(n+1)/n − 1, tending to 1 for large n and to the spherical equation for small n
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: although the shape factor is absent from the coverage equation, the coupling lets the cylinder and sphere penetrate deeper in coverage too; all three coverage profiles share their shape and front slope
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: a larger exposure lets larger particles be fully penetrated; as the radius grows the three geometries converge, because the 1/R and 2/R terms vanish
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: in the example the shape factor matters for radii below 600 µm, but the relevant size range depends on the exposure, not on a fixed size
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the slab and sphere estimates differ by under 5 % while ξ ≤ 0.15 and under 1 % while ξ ≤ 0.05; at full infiltration the difference reaches 40–45 %, so the shape factor matters more the deeper the coating
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: for the slab the penetration depth grows with the square root of the exposure; for the sphere the shell volume shrinks as r³ toward the centre, so the relation differs
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: τ/ε from 1 to 5 is typical of catalyst supports; more tortuosity or less porosity restricts diffusion, and with restricted diffusion the slab and sphere depths converge, while at low τ/ε the shrinking-core effect sets them apart
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: a heavier reactant penetrates less, since its thermal velocity is lower, as Yim et al. also found
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: a smaller areal site density, a smaller GPC, lengthens the penetration depth since fewer sites consume the reactant; at σ = 1 nm-2 the spheres are fully coated
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: a larger surface-to-pore-volume ratio s̄ means more adsorption sites per volume and a shorter penetration depth
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the sticking probability leaves the reactant density profiles nearly unchanged, as Keuter and Arts found; only near depletion does a lower β0 let the reactant travel slightly deeper, unlike the slight increase Yim et al. saw with their analytic pressure
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the pore diameter enters only through the Knudsen coefficient: a narrower pore restricts diffusion; r(θ=1/2) grows linearly with pore diameter, faster for the sphere (×2.5 from 10 to 40 nm) than the slab (×2)
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the coverage profiles widen as β0 falls; sphere and slab share the coverage shape for a given β0 and differ only in depth, since only the propagation geometry differs
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: with typical supports a higher specific surface area comes with more pore volume and smaller pores; at fixed exposure a higher surface area shortens the penetration depth and a larger pore diameter lengthens it through the Knudsen coefficient
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: with the reactant quantity fixed as a number density the penetration depth rises with temperature; with a fixed partial pressure the number density falls with temperature and so does the penetration depth, as Yim and Gayle reported
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol a: the geometry factor a = s + 1: outer surface area over particle volume, times R
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol A_O: specific surface area of the porous medium
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol A_Par: outer surface area of the particle as an ideal non-porous body
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol β0: initial sticking probability of the reactant on collision with the pore wall
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol D_e: effective diffusion coefficient in the pores, ε/τ times the Knudsen coefficient
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
definition_note: in the pores: porosity over tortuosity times the Knudsen coefficient

statement: symbol D_i: gas-phase diffusion coefficient, the Bosanquet sum
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol D_Kn: Knudsen diffusion coefficient
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol D_mi: molecular diffusion coefficient
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol d_pore: mean pore diameter of the porous medium
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
definition_note: the pore, the smallest opening the reactant passes

statement: symbol v_th: mean thermal velocity of the reactant
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol ε: porosity, the void fraction of the particle
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol GPC: growth per cycle
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol h: height of the cylinder
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol k_B: Boltzmann constant
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol m_r: mass of a single reactant molecule; Table 2 gives it as a molar mass
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol n_P0: volumetric reactant number density of the gas in the pores (n_P0 at the surface)
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
term: n_P0|n_p0|n_P|n_p|n_{P0}|volumetric reactant number density|reactant number density
definition_note: n_P0: the value at the particle surface

statement: symbol p_A0: partial pressure of the reactant A
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol r: radial coordinate from the outer surface (0) to the centre (R)
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol r_θ=1/2: the penetration depth: the radial position where the coverage is one half
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol R: particle radius (half-thickness for a slab), the diffusion path from the surface to the centre
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
definition_note: the radius: the depth the reactant must travel to the centre

statement: symbol s: shape factor s = a − 1: 0 slab, 1 cylinder, 2 sphere
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol s̄: the ratio of specific surface area to pore volume, s̄ = A_O/V_p, surface per pore volume
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol s_0: average area of one adsorption site, 1/σ
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol SCM: shrinking core model
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol σ: areal number density of metal atoms deposited per cycle at saturation, the GPC as a site density
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol t: reactant exposure time
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
term: t|reactant exposure time|exposure time|reactant exposure duration|exposure duration

statement: symbol τ: tortuosity of the pore network
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol T: ALD process temperature
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol θ: surface coverage, the fraction of occupied sites
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol V_P: pore volume per mass
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol V_Par: particle volume
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol τ/ε: the combined factor tortuosity over porosity, the reciprocal of the ε/τ of the effective diffusion coefficient
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol ξ: the normalized penetration depth ξ = r(θ=1/2)/R; one means a fully coated particle
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol exposure: the exposure, partial pressure times exposure time, in Pa s
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: symbol ALD: atomic layer deposition
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eq. (1): the diffusion-reaction equation for the reactant number density with the shape factor s in the radial Laplacian and the adsorption loss ¼ v_th β0 n_P (1 − θ), scaled by s̄ = A_O/V_p
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eqs. (2)-(3): the Bosanquet relation 1/D_i = 1/D_mi + 1/D_Kn, reduced to D_i = D_Kn for Knudsen-dominated transport
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eqs. (4)-(5): D_e = (ε/τ) D_Kn with the kinetic-theory Knudsen coefficient from the pore diameter, temperature and molecular mass
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eqs. (6)-(8): the equations for slab, cylinder and sphere, the latter two with D_e (1/R) and D_e (2/R) times the first derivative
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eq. (9): the coverage rate dθ/dt = −s0 ¼ v_th β0 n_P (1 − θ) with s0 = 1/σ; the ideal gas law converts the partial pressure to the number density
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eqs. (10)-(11): θ and n_p are zero everywhere at t = 0
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: Eqs. (12)-(13): Dirichlet n_p = n_p0 at the surface, Neumann zero gradient at the centre
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b

statement: the PDEs were solved in MATLAB R2023a by the method of lines: dss004 (five-point) and dss044 (six-point) finite differences, typically 300 radial points, ode15s for the stiff ODE system
author: 10.1039_d3cp05639b
